newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler fined for truck fuel system failure.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler fined for truck fuel system failure.

text.p: U.S. safety officials said Friday that Chrysler Corp paid a $140,000 civil penalty in connection with the failure of 1994 Dodge Ram trucks adequately to protect fuel systems in case of a crash.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said the Ram 1500 pick-up trucks with long wheelbase, lighter gauge frame rails and no rear bumpers failed the standard to protect the fuel system's integrity in a crash.
Because of this, 7,000 trucks were recalled, it said.
The NHTSA said Chrysler's development tests were not based on a "worst case" scenario and they should have raised the firm's awareness of the potential failure of the fuel system.
It said that in its own test, the cargo bed bent into a "V" shape and frame rails buckled, pinching the fuel filler hose and detaching the fuel filler neck.
The NHTSA said this allowed four times as much fuel to leak as the standard allowed, greatly increasing the possibility of a fire in a crash.
It said the $140,000 fine paid was among the top five penalties recovered for a federal safety standard violation.
The NHTSA said it sought a big fine because this was the second time in recent years that Chrysler made and sold trucks that failed the fuel system integrity standard.
